scope: Construction foundation pylon and fluid pipe graph DataVault descriptor sovereignty

problem.summary: FoundationPylonGpuBatch used a direct DataVault callback cast. FluidPipeGraphRuntime used direct previous/current DataVault casts and generic nonzero handle predicates for read-only, write-lock, ensure, release, and release-write-lock paths.
problem.risk: Fluid pipe graph owns 21 same-owner Construction lanes. Same-owner wrong-lane descriptors can target compatible primitive element types unless every helper proves the expected BufferID.

changes.detail: DataVault hot-swap now pattern-matches IDataVault instead of direct casting.
DataVault hot-swap now pattern-matches previous and current IDataVault services before releasing old buffers and rebinding.
Read-only consumers pass exact expected BufferIDs into TryReadOnlyBuffer.
Ensure, write-lock acquisition, write-lock release, buffer release, and helper predicates now require expected BufferID plus SystemID.Construction plus generation.

write_lock_proof.finally_release_note: Existing call sites release Solve locks in finally blocks through ReleaseSolveWriteLocks; this patch added exact BufferID gates before acquisition and release.

scoped_bad_pattern_scan.command: rg -n "currentService as IDataVault|previousService as IDataVault|handle\.BufferID != 0u|handle\.BufferID == 0u|IsVaultHandleCreated|IsValidVaultHandle|OwnerSystemID|TryAcquireWriteLock\([^\n]*&&|&&[^\n]*TryAcquireWriteLock" FoundationPylonGpuBatch.cs FluidPipeGraphRuntime.cs

git_diff_check.only_warning: LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it

scalability_and_cinematic_cheat.note: No pipe solver, rupture, atmosphere exchange, foundation SDF, GPU upload, or quality-scaling behavior changed. This patch only hardens native identity and hot-swap ownership.

resource_throttling.reason: CPU guard was above 50 percent and an external dotnet build was active.
